claims.statement: NodeViewToggle is a StereoModeToggle-style 80x36 two-segment gallery|node control (kViewTiles / kViewNodes icons, help key nodeViewToggle, setNodeView + onToggle callbacks) inserted LEFT of the preset bar in PluginHeader; the header seeds it from services_.prefs.getBool(UiPrefs::kNodeView, false) at construction.

The view choice persists as a plain UiPrefs key UiPrefs::kNodeView = "t3k.nodeView" (UiPrefs.h:68; stored as "true"/"false" strings, default false = gallery): PluginRoot::onNodeViewToggle writes prefs.setBool(kNodeView, nodeView) and calls main_.chainScreen().setView(nodeView).

ChainScreen grows a third view branch: setView(bool) hides the gallery and shows the node view (and back); the node view has NO DragScroller — ChainScreen::scroller() keeps returning gallery_.scroller() even while the node view is visible; closeDetail() restores whichever view nodeView_ says the user was in.
The node-view ticket added Help keys + entries: nodeViewToggle, nodeView, nodeEmptySlot, node, nodePower, nodeRemove, nodeMode.

The node view is a second, TOGGLEABLE views layer over the same ChainState the gallery draws (ticket ui-block-interface-draft.md): no new DSP — a slot's contents ARE the existing ChainBlocks re-arranged in ChainState lane order, and every mutation goes back through ChainStore so gallery and node view can never disagree. The old 4x3 snake grid (kColumns=4/kRows=3, 84x60 cells, Grid::slotNearest drops) was replaced 2026-10-15 by the signal-line grid.

The grid is ONE row of 10 slots (Row::kSlotCount = 10, Row::kLabelH = 18 label band under each square, NodeModel.h:34-36); a SECOND row of 10 appears only when the lane exceeds 10 blocks (NodeView::paint/resized compute nCells = 10 + (lane.size() > 10 ? 10 : 0)) so lanes of 10 or fewer render a single row. Cell i = lane item i (1:1 left-lane map); tail cells beyond the lane are EMPTY = a valid bypassed pass-through state (the key difference from the gallery, where every tile is an effect).

Cell paint states (the Q-Cortex/Line 6 transparency law): an ACTIVE block paints an opaque theme::kSurface fill (so the signal line STOPS at its edges) with kind-colour border at full alpha and white icon; a POWER-OFF block paints NO fill (the line runs THROUGH it) with border at 0.35 alpha and a muted icon; an EMPTY slot is invisible EXCEPT on mouse hover or when the whole lane is empty/insert-only (CellState.presetEmpty) — then a dashed border + plus glyph + 'add' label so the user knows where to click.

The signal line (NodeView::paint, ~:570-586) draws, per VISIBLE row, a 2 px white.withAlpha(0.45f) fillRect at the row's square-centre Y from rowX_ to W - rowX_, labelled 'In'/'Out' in the gutters, and it is painted BEFORE the cells so cells paint over it — active squares' opaque fill stops it, power-off/empty squares let it run through. It is painted only when nodeView_ is set.

Repaint invariants (bug found in the 2026-10-15 capture hunt — the line stayed invisible for a whole debug session): setNodeView(bool) (NodeView.cpp:412) and chainChanged() (NodeView.cpp:419) both END WITH repaint(), because refresh() only updates the cell children; the body (signal line, In/Out labels, strip) must repaint on first-time activation, on lane row gain/loss, and on selection change or the line silently stays absent until an unrelated invalidate.

NodeStrip is the selected block's SINGLE-ROW parameter strip (44 px stacked header, kStripHeadH = 44, NodeView.cpp:54) in Line 6 stadium style: the per-knob VALUE readout paints persistently ABOVE the knob face (NodeStrip::values_ filled with KnobScale::format(knobFromStored(*scale, raw)) — the real-unit value, not the 0..1 stored one; passing the stored value produced the '-1776.0 dB' / '-922337203…' garbage), while the knob's own name label sits below it (Knob Options labelOnTop = true). Stacked header: block-kind label in caps (titleFont) over the mode line (Delay/Compressor/Reverb::modeName or the kind name) in the kind accent colour — display-only; mode cycling lives in the cell right-click menu. Panel is contained + centred (jmin(W - 16, 1100) wide), theme::kPanelBg @ 0.55 tinted fill, 10 px radius. Knobs are owned std::vector<Knob*> (created on selection, deleted in clearContent()); their onChange writes back through chain.setBlockParam(id, param, knobToStored(...)). Params come from the SHARED paramsFor table in views/gallery/EffectParams.h (tone nodes show only In/Out/Mix trims).

Pointer grammar on a node: a short click selects the block (params load into the strip); a 250 ms hold (kHoldMs = 250, NodeView.cpp:58) begins a lane drag; motion before the hold cancels the timer; right-click opens the block menu (power toggle, help key nodePower; remove, help key nodeRemove; plus the palette add-menu over Model::paletteKinds()). Drags use juce::Component::createComponentSnapshot ghosts (JUCE 9 API) and a suppress-click-until timestamp keeps a drop from firing a stray select; drops commit through chain.reorderBlocks with the spliced full-lane id list.

Persistence: UiPrefs::kNodeView = "t3k.nodeView" (UiPrefs.h:68) is a plain STRING pref "true"/"false" — UiPrefs::getBool accepts only those two spellings, anything else (including JUCE var::toString()'s "1") falls back to the default false. ChainScreen's ctor reads it and calls setView(true) when set; PluginRoot::onNodeViewToggle (fired by the PluginHeader NodeViewToggle, an 80x36 two-segment gallery|node control, help key nodeViewToggle) writes the pref and forwards to chainScreen().setView(nodeView). ChainScreen::setView hides the gallery / shows the node view; the node view has no DragScroller.

Testbed: the node-main scenario (scenarios.json) carries a 3-block left lane (compressor selected, chorus, insert) and seeds "localStorage": {"t3k.nodeView": "true"} so the node view is the visible surface. TWO landmines: (1) the seed value MUST be the string "true" — Host::seedPrefs does prefs.set(name, value.toString()) and a JSON bool becomes "1", which getBool rejects (the signal line stayed invisible for the whole 2026-10-15 capture hunt until this was fixed); (2) UiTestbed --capture <outDir> <scenario> is what writes PNGs (--selftest does not), and --capture auto-iterates all scenarios, so node-main gets a golden with no Main.cpp change.
